title: Email content NLP features (subject + body)
hypothesis: The champion uses zero email-side features. Subject-line length, presence of urgency cues, sentiment polarity, and body length should add signal because email_popularity_pair AUC (0.81) reveals strong email-level variance that no user-history feature captures.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: highest novelty — fills the entire email-feature gap. Reach via 67% email-attribution rate and email_popularity AUC of 0.81.

title: User x email topic affinity (historical action match)
hypothesis: For each (user, email) pair, build features measuring the user prior action rate on emails matching the current email topic/keywords. Non-streak-users AUC of 0.644 suggests the model fails on users whose actions are topic-driven rather than habit-driven.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: novel cross-feature (user x email) that directly targets non-streak-user weakness (0.644 vs 0.6755 pooled).

title: User account tenure and signup-cohort features
hypothesis: Cold-start AUC of 0.658 underperforms pooled (0.6755). Adding account_age_days, signup_source, lifetime_emails_received, and signup_cohort_year should help the model distinguish new-engaged from long-dormant users beyond raw lifetime_actions_prior.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: targets cold-start gap. Lower novelty than email-side features but high signal certainty from year-over-year drift open question in GOAL.md.

title: Email send-timing features (day-of-week and hour-of-send)
hypothesis: Walk-forward fold variance (std 0.022, range 0.604-0.692) suggests time-varying effects. Day-of-week, hour-of-day, and gap-since-last-send features should capture cadence and fatigue signals invisible to the current actioning-history-only feature set.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: temporal features address fold-variance heterogeneity. Diverse from user-history features.

title: Sender and campaign reputation features
hypothesis: Sender-side features (sender_id, sender_prior_action_rate, campaign_size, days_since_sender_last_active) capture organization-level email quality variance that email_popularity residualization removes from labels but not from features.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: novel domain (org/sender) but risk of overlap with email_popularity confound. Worth one shot.

reason: Stacked upstream contract mismatch between libs/run_record.py and civic_shout project: (1) libs/run_record.py:191 passes outcome_version kwarg to eda(), but civic_shout's eda() in projects/civic_shout_action_rate_increase/eda/__init__.py:800 does not accept it; (2) libs/ledgers.LedgerWriter.assert_managed requires a _managed_by sentinel as line 1 of results.jsonl, but existing run_01_smoke rows were written via direct open().write() without that header. Both fixer surfaces are in the forbidden-write list (eda.py, libs/**, results.jsonl-via-direct-write). Feature family email_content_nlp itself was built successfully: 4634 emails, 11 features (body length, urgency/CTA keyword counts, exclamation density, uppercase ratio, first-line proxy), 0.24s wall, local parquet at data/projects/civic_shout_action_rate_increase/features/email_content_nlp/v1.parquet. Next iteration needs civic_shout eda() updated to accept outcome_version and results.jsonl re-sentineled before run_record(...) is usable here.

hypothesis: The champion uses zero email-side features. Subject-line length, presence of urgency cues, sentiment polarity, and body length should add signal because email_popularity_pair AUC (0.81) reveals strong email-level variance that no user-history feature captures.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: highest novelty — fills the entire email-feature gap. Reach via 67% email-attribution rate and email_popularity AUC of 0.81.

title: Email-user semantic affinity via content embeddings
hypothesis: Embed each email (subject+body) and each user history of acted-on emails; for each (user,email) pair, feature = cosine similarity between current email embedding and user prior-action embedding centroid. Distinct from naive topic matching by capturing semantic similarity. Targets non-streak-users AUC of 0.644 by encoding is-this-email-like-the-ones-this-user-historically-signs.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: novel cross-feature (semantic embedding x user history). Directly attacks non-streak-users gap (0.644 vs 0.6755 pooled). Mechanically distinct from bs-iter2-01 (token/length NLP stats) and bs-iter2-02 (keyword topic match) by using dense embeddings.

title: User geographic and locale features
hypothesis: Petition and civic-action behavior is geographically heterogeneous (state issues, regional campaigns, time-zone send-receive offsets). Adding user state, country, time-zone, and locale should capture variance unrelated to user action history, including cold-start (AUC 0.658) and walk-forward fold variance.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: orthogonal feature dimension (no overlap with any of the 5 existing ideas). Modest novelty, modest expected signal. Cheap probe of cold-start gap (0.658).

title: Exponentially weighted recency action features
hypothesis: Champion uses raw actioned_last_N counts at fixed N in 1,3,5,10. Replacing with exponentially decayed counts at multiple half-lives (3-day, 14-day, 60-day) plus continuous days-since-last-action should sharpen the recency signal beyond fixed-window step functions and reduce fold variance.
tier_rationale: EXPLORE: refinement of existing actioned_last_N family but mechanistically distinct (continuous decay vs step). Targets walk-forward fold std of 0.022. Low cost and low risk; complements rather than substitutes existing features.

reason: Same upstream blocker as iter 2 (bailed_unfeasible). The feature email_user_semantic_affinity v1 was built and validated successfully (smoke-tier cache: 129,019 rows, history scan over 36.7M rows for 100k sampled users, 57.2s wall, local parquet at data/projects/civic_shout_action_rate_increase/features/email_user_semantic_affinity/v1.parquet). run_03.py was written following the run_02 pattern with sample(0.001, seed=42) on the date-filtered user_emails frame (mirrored verbatim in create_cache so join keys align). Executing run_03 fails inside run_record() at libs/run_record.py:185-191 with TypeError: eda() got an unexpected keyword argument 'outcome_version' — libs/run_record.py passes outcome_version, but projects/civic_shout_action_rate_increase/eda/__init__.py:800 defines eda(data, feature_cols, outcome_variable, eda_config) with no outcome_version parameter and no **kwargs. Cascading: the failure-shell-row writer (libs/ledgers.LedgerWriter.assert_managed) also blocks because results.jsonl lacks a _managed_by sentinel as line 1 (legacy run_01_smoke rows were appended via direct open().write()). Both fixer surfaces (libs/run_record.py, projects/civic_shout_action_rate_increase/eda/__init__.py, and the un-sentineled results.jsonl) are on this session's forbidden-write list. Next iteration needs the supervisor to (a) add outcome_version as an accepted/ignored kwarg on civic_shout eda(), and (b) re-sentinel results.jsonl + eda_results.jsonl + discovery_results.jsonl with the _managed_by header LedgerWriter expects.
